verdictJustification: Two toolchain candidates were tried on THIS machine, neither compatible, for two different real reasons: (1) the native Xcode 26.6/Swift 6.3.3 install, tried against two different real corpus projects (swift-argument-parser, swift-numerics), independently, with two different real Muter compile-failure signatures; (2) a swiftly-managed Swift 5.9.2 compiler layered on the same machine's only SDK (Xcode 26.6's macOS 26.5 SDK), classified compilerSDKIncompatible. A standalone Swift 5.9 compiler is insufficient on this machine; a matching older SDK (bundled with an old Xcode) is also required, and none is installed locally, and none was installed system-wide this session (deliberately, pending explicit authorization for a system-modifying multi-GB download). A COMPATIBLE toolchain was subsequently found and confirmed on GitHub Actions' macos-14 runner image (Xcode 15.2 / Swift 5.9.2 compiler / macOS 14.2 SDK, all matched) -- see Benchmarks/results/compatibility/xcode-15.2-swift-5.9-macos-14/gate-result.json for the full, real, passing gate run (workflow run 30963516384). This does NOT retroactively make this machine's own two candidates compatible -- both remain recorded as incompatible, exactly as observed. The verdict here reflects only this machine's own local state.

candidatesExplored.failureReason: Muter itself builds and its --version runs, but muter run fails to complete a real mutation run on every corpus project attempted under this toolchain. swift-argument-parser: 'ambiguous implicit access level for import of Foundation; it is imported as internal elsewhere' across multiple mutated files, ending in a fatalError. swift-numerics (clean checkout): got further (33 compile steps) before a separate fatalError compiling IntegerUtilities/ShiftWithRounding.swift. Muter's own repository was NOT patched to work around either failure, per explicit instruction -- the official pinned commit was used exactly as-is. mutantKitRunSucceeded is recorded false here too: MutantKit's own plan succeeded (417 mutations) and its run was genuinely executing, but was deliberately stopped before completion once Muter had already failed twice, since no comparison could result either way -- this is honestly a non-completion, not a MutantKit failure, and is not counted as a compatibility success for that reason alone (isCompatible requires a completed run from both tools).

classification: compilerSDKIncompatible (never muterCompileFailed -- this candidate never reached Muter at all). Installed swiftly (Homebrew, official swiftlang formula) and `swiftly install 5.9.2`; the resulting toolchain is selectable via `TOOLCHAINS=org.swift.592202312111a xcrun swift --version`, confirmed reporting 5.9.2. But `TOOLCHAINS` only swaps the compiler frontend -- the macOS SDK still comes from DEVELOPER_DIR (Xcode 26.6, macOS 26.5 SDK, the only Xcode on this machine). That SDK's Foundation.swiftinterface uses typed-throws syntax (`throws(E)`), a Swift 6 language feature the 5.9.2 frontend cannot parse: `error: emit-module command failed due to signal 6` / `error: expected ',' separator` inside Foundation.swiftmodule/arm64e-apple-macos.swiftinterface:1954. Isolated precisely: a Foundation-free Swift target builds cleanly under the identical TOOLCHAINS=5.9.2 env; the failure is specific to Foundation's module interface. Since XCTest itself links Foundation, and every real corpus project (and almost certainly Muter's and MutantKit's own fixtures) touches Foundation, this blocks the whole approach before Muter or MutantKit were ever invoked -- neither tool's own build/run fields apply (recorded null, not false, since neither was actually attempted).

muterOwnRequirement.note: Both real compile failures observed are consistent with a Swift-5.9-targeted codebase failing to compile under Swift 6.3's stricter import-access and other language-mode checks. No .github/workflows directory was found in Muter's repository tree, so its own CI toolchain pin (if any) was not discoverable this way; the swift-tools-version declaration is recorded here as the best available real evidence and is now tracked in Benchmarks/manifest.json's toolchainRequirements.

unrecoverableRuns.note: Not classified as timeout, crash, or success -- none were observed. There was no process left to inspect (flat CPU or otherwise); the run's own working state (task, PID, log, and its parent directory) did not survive into this session. This is a separate, later run than the one recorded in mutantKitRunSucceeded above (which documents a real, deliberately-stopped-not-completed run on the same project).

nextSteps: This machine has no installable-without-system-modification alternate toolchain (no swiftly/xcodes, no Homebrew Swift formula, no existing /Library or ~/Library toolchain bundle).

Installing an older Xcode or a swift.org standalone 5.9 toolchain was deliberately NOT attempted this session -- it is a system-modifying, likely-privileged action, and installing/downloading a multi-GB toolchain was judged out of scope for this benchmark run without explicit user confirmation.

The compatibility-lane harness code (BenchmarkToolchainProfile, ToolchainEnvironmentBuilder, ToolchainDiscovery, ToolchainDriftGuard, result-path isolation) is complete and unit-tested; it will run correctly the moment a second, Swift-5.9-capable toolchain becomes available on this or another machine.
